set.descent_text: This is a short crack in one of the small cliff bands below the east face, not a line to the summit. Build an anchor in a horizontal crack high on the slabs above the crack, then walk off from there and rejoin the trail around the east side of the peak.

review.notes: Route page says the crack is a short line in a cliffband below the east face and parties can walk off.

set.approach: Start from the Fourth of July trailhead and hike the Arapaho Pass trail to Lake Dorothy at the pass. The route is on an unnamed peak just north of Mount Neva, rising west of the lake out of a snowfield. Go around the south side of the lake to the toe of that peak, then climb the snowfield to the right of the big freestanding pyramid-shaped block at the base of the face, where the first pitch starts.
set.descent_text: From the top, walk and scramble to the flat summit area then find the ledge on the right-hand side marked by two upright pointed rocks. Bolted rappel anchors there lead down to a ledge with dark rock and a second set of anchors, and another rappel reaches the snowfield; two ropes are needed. Alternatively, take the fourth-class ridge down to Arapaho Pass, or keep going up the ridge to Mount Neva and descend one of its faces.

review.notes: Route page gives the approach from the trailhead and three descent options; rappel counts and lengths left out (one source).

set.approach: Hike the Pawnee Pass trail beyond Lake Isabelle, watching for the point where the south side of the prominent pinnacle sitting on the ridge between Little Pawnee and Pawnee Peak appears. Leave the trail and bushwhack across a boulderfield toward the face, then start at the left (west) end of the feature beside a big gully, at a clean corner with a seam.
set.descent_text: The route ends on the ridge in the middle of the Little Pawnee to Pawnee traverse, reached by a final stretch of fourth-class hiking behind the pinnacle on its north side. From there, either continue west along the ridge, which probably takes longer but is easier, or return east, which is probably quicker but has fourth-class steps.

review.notes: Route page gives the approach line and where the route ends.

set.approach: Work in from the far right side, scrambling along the ledges and up the approach ramp. On the way are an exposed bulge and a low-angle fifth-class slab, and some parties rope up before the bulge. Roughly 200 feet before the top of the ramp, look for a little cave plus an unobtrusive pillar; the first pitch starts on that pillar.
set.descent_text: Parties either walk off via the Southeast Gully or Hourglass Ridge, or rappel the route. For the rappel, the top pitch can be rappelled on a single 60 m rope, and the lower pitches can be descended by following the route down from the fourth-pitch anchor, with a direct double-rope rappel that skips the two hardest pitches.

review.notes: Route page gives the ramp approach and the walk-off or rappel options.

set.approach: From Emerald Lake, contour around the north side of the lake heading west toward the obvious tower. Either climb snow or talus west onto the ledges across the spire's south face, which skips the first pitch, or go up Dragon's Tail Couloir until you can reach the same ledge from the east. The route starts in a chimney beside a prominent crack.
set.descent_text: From the summit, walk north a short way until the arete to Flattop Mountain comes into view. Rather than downclimbing and following the arete, use the rappel station and descend east into Dragon's Tail Couloir onto a grassy ledge system, where the technical ground ends. Follow the ledges north, scramble to the top of the couloir, and hike down the Flattop trail.

review.notes: Route page gives the Emerald Lake approach and the rappel-and-trail descent.

set.approach: Climb Dragon's Tail Couloir to the start. The first moves are in a cleft, with a big boulder resting against the wall to its left.

review.notes: Route page says the start is reached by climbing the couloir; no descent given.

set.descent_text: Rappel the southeast side of the spire in short rappels, then scramble down into the valley south of the spire and follow it back toward the start of Walk of Life. The area is remote.

review.notes: Route page gives the descent; count and rope length left out.

set.descent_text: Rappel from slings at the boulders on top, pass south through the slot at the back of the main pinnacle, and finish with bolted rappels to the ground.

review.notes: Route page gives the descent; rappel count and rope left out.

set.descent_text: The route finishes on the north summit. Go down a short rappel or downclimb in the chimney at the north summit's south end to reach to the broad terrace under the south summit spire. That terrace is the top of the descent chimney, which goes down the west (back) side of the formation.

review.notes: Route page gives the top-out and descent path; the Anus Grape page agrees on the terrace and the chimney.

set.descent_text: The route joins the last pitch of Solar Winds to the north summit; an easier finish over moderate ground reaches the terrace below the south summit spire. That terrace is the top of the descent chimney, which goes down the west (back) side of the formation.

review.notes: Route page says it joins Solar Winds to the north summit; terrace and descent chimney named there and on the Solar Winds page.

set.descent_text: Walk off the top, heading climber's right (west), and scramble down the class 4 approach ground back to the base. If a rope is left fixed in the chimney, keep it coiled so it cannot fall into the chimney, which snags ropes.
